item.title: [Featured Article] Aucanquilcha
item.description: Aucanquilcha is a large compound volcano in the Antofagasta Region of northern Chile, within the Central Volcanic Zone of the Andes. The volcano has the form of a ridge reaching an altitude of 6,176 metres (20,262 ft) above sea level, formed between 1.04 and 0.23 million years ago; there is ongoing fumarolic activity. The volcano is part of a larger cluster of volcanoes sometimes known as the "Aucanquilcha cluster" or "Aucanquilcha complex". This cluster includes lava domes and lava flows that have formed in several stages over 11 million years of activity with varying magma output. During the ice ages, Aucanquilcha was covered in an ice cap that left moraines and cirques.

item.title: [In the News] Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns amidst allegations of being targeted by a Chinese spy and of having extramarital affairs.
item.description: Jen-Hsun "Jensen" Huang is a Taiwanese and American electrical engineer and businessman. He co-founded the technology company Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable corporations, and served as its president and CEO from its founding in 1993 until his resignation in November 2026. As of November 2026, Forbes estimates his net worth at over US$150 billion, making him the eleventh-wealthiest person in the world.

item.title: [In the News] The Salvadoran military intervention in Haiti intensifies with an airstrike on 400 Mawozo's alleged headquarters and a deployment to Stade Sylvio Cator.
item.description: Since 21 October 2026, El Salvador has been conducting a military intervention in Haiti following a gang ambush on 18 October that resulted in four Salvadoran aviation technicians of the Gang Suppression Force (GSF) being kidnapped. According to Salvadoran president Nayib Bukele, the intervention's primary objective is to rescue the four technicians, while threatening to "finish" the Haitian gangs if the technicians are not rescued alive.

item.title: [In the News] American ocean liner SS United States is scuttled in the Gulf of Mexico to create the largest artificial reef.
item.description: SS United States was an American ocean liner that was built during 1950 and 1951 for the United States Lines. She was the largest ocean liner to be entirely constructed in the United States and the fastest ocean liner to cross the Atlantic Ocean in either direction, earning the Blue Riband for the highest average speed since her maiden voyage in 1952, a title that remains uncontested.

item.title: [In the News] The End of Everything by M. John Harrison wins the Booker Prize.
item.description: The End of Everything is a post-apocalyptic novel by English author M. John Harrison, first published in the UK in 2026 by Serpent's Tail. Harrison's 13th novel, it won the 2026 Booker Prize.

item.title: [In the News] Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia's oldest and most prominent independent newspapers, closes under pressure from the Russian authorities.
item.description: Novaya Gazeta was a independent Russian newspaper. It became known for its critical and investigative coverage of Russian political and social affairs, the Chechen wars, corruption among the ruling elite, and increasing authoritarianism in Russia. It was published in Moscow with print editions on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays until shortly after the beginning of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine, after which Novaya Gazeta appeared online only. English-language articles on the website were published on a weekly basis in the form of the Russia, Explained newsletter. As of 2023, the newspaper had a daily print circulation of 108,000, and online visits of 613,000.

item.title: [Most Read #2] Ramayana: Part 1
item.description: Daily Views: 618,656 — Ramayana: Part 1 is a 2026 Indian Hindi-language epic mythological film directed by Nitesh Tiwari, who co-wrote the screenplay with Shridhar Raghavan. Produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, the film is based on the Hindu epic Ramayana by Valmiki. It is the first instalment of a two-part film series, with Part 1 being based on the first three kāṇḍa (chapters) of Ramayana, which chronicle the life of Prince Rama from childhood up to his adventurous 14-year exile. The first part features an ensemble cast that includes Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi, Ravi Dubey, Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan, and Lara Dutta.

item.title: [Most Read #3] Colette Kress
item.description: Daily Views: 279,241 — Colette Marie Kress is an American business executive. She has been the interim chief executive officer (CEO) of Nvidia since November 12, 2026, following the resignation of former Nvidia CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang amid a scandal.

item.title: [Most Read #4] Nvidia
item.description: Daily Views: 252,871 — Nvidia Corporation is an American multinational technology company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. The company develops graphics processing units (GPUs), systems on chips (SoCs), and application programming interfaces (APIs) for gaming, data science, high-performance computing, artificial intelligence (AI) hardware, and mobile and automotive applications. Founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem, Nvidia is among the largest companies by market capitalization.

item.title: [Most Read #5] Chris Van Hollen
item.description: Daily Views: 204,913 — Christopher Van Hollen Jr., also known as CVH, is an American attorney and politician serving as the senior United States senator from Maryland, a seat he has held since 2017. A member of the Democratic Party, he served as the U.S. representative for Maryland's 8th congressional district from 2003 to 2017 and as a Maryland state senator from 1995 to 2003. He is currently contesting Chuck Schumer in the 2026 Senate Democratic Caucus leadership election.

item.title: [Most Read #6] Piracy
item.description: Daily Views: 201,972 — Piracy is an act of robbery or criminal violence by ship or boat-borne attackers upon another ship or a coastal area, typically intending to steal cargo and valuable goods, or take hostages. Those who conduct acts of piracy are called pirates, and vessels used for piracy are called pirate ships. The earliest documented instances of piracy date to the 14th century BC, when the Sea Peoples, a group of ocean raiders, attacked the ships of the Aegean and Mediterranean civilizations. Narrow channels which funnel shipping into predictable routes have long created opportunities for piracy, as well as for privateering and commerce raiding.

item.title: [Most Read #7] Alice Huang (executive)
item.description: Daily Views: 200,012 — Alice Huang is a Chinese technology executive and investor. She is an executive at Megaspeed, a Singaporean technology company.

item.title: [Most Read #8] Sam Hartman
item.description: Daily Views: 191,577 — Samuel Hartman is an American professional football quarterback for the Washington Commanders of the National Football League (NFL). Hartman played five seasons of college football for the Wake Forest Demon Deacons, setting several school records and finishing as the all-time passing touchdowns leader in Atlantic Coast Conference (ACC) history. He played with the Notre Dame Fighting Irish in 2023 before signing with the Commanders as an undrafted free agent in 2024.

item.title: [Most Read #9] Mauricio Pochettino
item.description: Daily Views: 172,224 — Mauricio Roberto Pochettino Trossero is an Argentine professional football manager and former footballer who is the head coach of the United States national team. He will become head coach of Premier League club Manchester United on 18 November 2026.

item.title: [Most Read #10] List of highest-grossing Indian films
item.description: Daily Views: 171,338 — This ranking lists the highest-grossing Indian films produced by Indian cinema, based on conservative global box office estimates as reported by organisations classified as green by Wikipedia. The figures are not adjusted for inflation. However, there is no official tracking of figures and sources publishing data are frequently pressured to increase their estimates.
